+# Checks on the pull request title and description. Findings appear in the summary comment.
+# Exact formats (ticket id pattern, Conventional Commits prefix) are better checked with a regex in CI;
+# these rules cover what needs reading: is the title specific, does the description explain why.
+context:
+  include_pr_body: true
+
+rules:
+  - id: pr.title-specific
+    description: Title does not say what the change does
+    type: noul
+    scope: pr
+    severity: minor
+    locate: false
+    fires_on: "no"
+    instructions: >-
+      Ignoring markers such as WIP, Draft or DO NOT MERGE, does `pr.title` say what the change
+      does and which part of the system it affects, specifically enough that a teammate could
+      tell what changed without opening the pull request?
+    criteria:
+      true: 'Specific titles such as "Add CSV export to the invoices list", "WIP: payment retries with backoff" or "Fix token refresh race in the auth client".'
+      false: Generic or empty titles such as "Fix bug", "Updates", "Changes", "Small fixes", a bare ticket number or a branch name like "feature/user-search".
+
+  - id: pr.title-unfinished
+    description: Title marks the change as unfinished
+    type: noul
+    scope: pr
+    severity: major
+    locate: false
+    instructions: >-
+      Does `pr.title` mark the change as unfinished or not ready to merge, for example with WIP,
+      DO NOT MERGE, DNM, draft, temp or "not ready"?

+    description: $effect starts a listener, timer, subscription or observer without returning a cleanup
+    type: noul
+    severity: major
+    paths: ["{{vars.svelte_paths}}"]
+    instructions: >-
+      Is there an added Svelte `$effect(() => { ... })` block in `changes.lines` whose body
+      starts something that keeps running (addEventListener, setInterval, setTimeout, a
+      subscribe or on* subscription, or a ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver or
+      MutationObserver), and whose body does not return a function that removes, clears,
+      unsubscribes or disconnects it?
+    criteria:
+      true: Inside the $effect body a listener, timer, subscription or observer is created and the effect has no return statement that undoes it.
+      false: >-
+        No $effect is added, the $effect only reads or assigns state, or it returns a cleanup:
+        a function (return () => ...), a variable holding the unsubscribe function
+        (return unsub), or the result of the subscribe call itself
+        (return window.api.onSomething(...), which returns its unsubscribe function).
+        Timers and listeners outside $effect do not count.

pr.title: fix(updater): bypass unreliable quitAndInstall on macOS
pr.body:
## Summary

- Bypass `MacUpdater.quitAndInstall()` on macOS which silently hangs when Squirrel.Mac hasn't finished its separate download, causing the app to restart without applying the update
- Use `app.releaseSingleInstanceLock()` + `app.relaunch()` + `app.quit()` on macOS — lets `autoInstallOnAppQuit` handle the update during normal quit cycle
- Add early return in `before-quit` handler during update to avoid interfering with Squirrel's install process
- Add "Installing update…" UI state to prevent re-clicks and show progress

## Test plan

- [ ] Build packaged macOS app, trigger update, click "Restart Now" — app should show "Installing update…", quit, and relaunch with the new version
- [ ] Verify window session is restored after update restart
- [ ] Verify the 10s safety timeout forces exit if quit hangs
- [ ] Verify normal quit (non-update) still works correctly with active session warning

pr.title: feat(ui): shared Markdown component and in-app attachment viewer
pr.body:
## What

Two UX fixes reported from live usage:

- **Markdown rendered everywhere through one component.** New `shared/Markdown.svelte` — sanitized (marked + DOMPurify, GFM with newline-as-break) with self-contained typography (headings, lists, code, tables, blockquotes, task-list checkboxes) scaled by the consumer's text-size class. Converted call sites:
  - task description and comments in the Task panel (previously raw `whitespace-pre-wrap` text),
  - PR body in the PR details modal (same),
  - changelog entries and the About license (previously per-dialog `marked` + `DOMPurify` pipelines — now deduplicated).
  The notes pane keeps its contenteditable preview — it is an editor with its own input/paste handling, not a display surface. Link clicks stay safe with no local handling: the main process blocks top-level navigation and routes safe external URLs to the OS browser.
- **Task attachments open in-app instead of the external browser.** Clicking an attachment opens a focus-trapped lightbox (Esc/backdrop close): images render directly from the authenticated proxy (fetched on demand when the thumbnail preview has not loaded yet), non-images show a save hint. **Save…** to disk is the primary action; open-in-tracker is demoted to an icon.
- New `taskTracker:attachmentSave` IPC mirrors the hardened `attachmentPreview` addressing: the renderer supplies only task key + attachment id, provider metadata decides URL and filename; the native save dialog is shown before any download and the suggested filename is sanitized of path-like characters.

## Why

Task descriptions, comments, and PR bodies displayed raw markdown markup; three dialogs each had their own parse pipeline. Attachments could only be opened in an external browser with no way to save them from Canopy.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev`, open a worktree linked to a tracker task with a markdown description/comments → both render formatted (headers, lists, code).
2. GIT section → View PR → the description renders as markdown.
3. Task panel → click an image attachment → in-app lightbox; **Save…** writes the file where you choose; the external-link icon still opens the tracker. Click a non-image attachment → same dialog with the save hint.
4. Help → About and the post-update changelog still render correctly (now through the shared component).
5. `npm test` (105 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run lint`.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [ ] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default) — n/a, UI fix of existing features
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell commands
- [x] Keyboard accessible (lightbox: focus trap, Escape, labelled buttons)
- [x] IPC follows `feature:action` naming and uses `invoke`/`handle`
- [x] Renderer code does not import Node.js modules directly
- [x] Feature docs in `docs/` updated (`docs/integrations/task-tracker.md`)

pr.title: build(deps): upgrade Electron 41 to 42
pr.body:
## What

Bumps `electron` ^41.0.0 → **^42.4.1** (latest stable: Chromium 148, Node 24.16, V8 14.8). Supersedes the failed Dependabot PR #273.

## Why

Improves security posture (current Electron/Chromium). The earlier #273 failed CI on a native-module build error against V8 14.8 — **root cause was `better-sqlite3@12.8.0` having no Electron 42 build target, not Electron or node-pty**. `better-sqlite3` is now at ^12.11.1 (landed via #281's grouped bump), which adds the Electron 42 target, so the from-source rebuild during `electron-builder install-app-deps` now succeeds. node-pty is Node-API (ABI-stable) and needed no change.

electron-vite 5 / electron-builder 26 / electron-updater 6 all already support Electron 42. No source changes required — the only 41→42 behavior note (macOS `UNNotification`) is satisfied by the signed + notarized production build.

## Checklist

- [x] Clean `npm install` + `electron-builder install-app-deps` — better-sqlite3 + node-pty rebuilt against V8 14.8, **no ABI errors** (the step that failed #273)
- [x] `npm run build` — exit 0 (typecheck + electron-vite build)
- [x] `npm audit` — 0 vulnerabilities
- [x] No source changes needed (breaking-change audit of src/main + src/preload clean)
- [ ] Packaged smoke (PTY, SQLite stores, auto-update init, crashReporter, macOS notifications) + `test:e2e` — **pending, requires packaged/device run**
